plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked comparison diagram contrasts the 'Tyranny of Numbers' (thousands of hand-soldered discrete transistors, resistors, and capacitors) against Jack Kilby's 12 September 1958 monolithic germanium oscillator chip and Jean Hoerni & Robert Noyce's 23 January 1959 planar silicon integrated circuit with photolithographically printed aluminium interconnects.

teach_overlay.label: TYRANNY OF NUMBERS VS 12 SEP 1958 KILBY & 23 JAN 1959 NOYCE IC
teach_overlay.detail: Inked comparison diagram on period paper of the 'Tyranny of Numbers' (thousands of hand-soldered discrete parts) vs Jack Kilby's 12 September 1958 monolithic germanium chip and Robert Noyce's 23 January 1959 planar silicon integrated circuit
teach_overlay.scale: instead of soldering 100,000 separate parts together by hand, Noyce's planar chip printed the entire circuit flat onto a sliver of silicon like pages on a printing press
